question: What does the CSS selector "div > p" select?
explanation: The ">" combinator selects only direct children, not all descendants.

question: What does the CSS :nth-child(2n+1) selector match?
explanation: :nth-child(2n+1) matches elements at positions 1, 3, 5, etc. (odd positions). It is equivalent to :nth-child(odd).

question: What is CSS specificity and how is it calculated?
options: A weight system determining which CSS rules apply: inline > ID > class > element
The order in which CSS files are loaded
The number of properties in a rule
How specific a CSS property name is
explanation: Specificity determines which CSS rule wins when multiple rules target the same element. It is calculated as: inline styles (1000) > IDs (100) > classes/attributes/pseudo-classes (10) > elements/pseudo-elements (1).

question: What is the CSS "cascade" in Cascading Style Sheets?
options: The algorithm that resolves conflicts when multiple CSS rules apply to the same element
The order of CSS file imports
How styles flow from parent to child elements
explanation: The cascade is the algorithm that determines which styles to apply when multiple rules could apply to an element. It considers importance, specificity, and source order.

question: What does "box-sizing: border-box" do?
options: Makes width and height include padding and border
Creates a border around all elements
Changes the box model to use margins
Sets the element to block display
explanation: border-box makes the width and height properties include content, padding, and border, making layout calculations more intuitive.

question: What is the difference between margin and padding?
options: Margin is space outside the border; padding is space inside the border
Margin is for inline elements; padding is for block elements
They are identical but with different names
Padding is outside; margin is inside
explanation: Margin creates space between elements (outside the border). Padding creates space between content and the border (inside).

question: How does "position: sticky" work?
options: The element scrolls normally until reaching a threshold, then becomes fixed
The element is always fixed at the top
The element sticks to its parent container
The element cannot be scrolled past
explanation: position: sticky toggles between relative and fixed positioning. The element is relative until it crosses a specified threshold (top, bottom, etc.), then becomes fixed.

question: What is a CSS custom property (variable)?
options: A property defined with -- prefix that can store reusable values
A property that changes automatically based on viewport
A JavaScript variable that controls CSS
explanation: CSS custom properties (--my-color: blue) store values that can be referenced with var(--my-color) throughout stylesheets, enabling maintainable theming.

question: What does "justify-content: space-between" do in Flexbox?
options: Distributes items evenly with the first item at the start and last item at the end
Centers all items with equal space
Pushes all items to the left
Adds space only between the first and last items
explanation: space-between distributes flex items evenly along the main axis, with no space before the first item or after the last item.

question: What is the difference between "align-items" and "align-content" in Flexbox?
options: align-items aligns items within a single line; align-content aligns wrapped lines within the container
align-content works on individual items; align-items works on the container
align-items is for horizontal; align-content is for vertical
explanation: align-items aligns flex items along the cross axis within each flex line. align-content aligns the flex lines themselves when there are multiple lines (flex-wrap).

question: What does "flex: 1 1 auto" mean?
explanation: The flex shorthand sets flex-grow (1 = grow to fill), flex-shrink (1 = can shrink), and flex-basis (auto = use content/width as initial size).

question: What does the "order" property do in Flexbox?
options: Changes the visual rendering order of flex items without modifying the DOM
Defines the sort order of a list
explanation: The order property controls the visual order of flex items. Lower values appear first. Default is 0. This is purely visual and does not affect DOM order or tab navigation.

question: What does "flex-wrap: wrap" do?
options: Allows flex items to wrap onto multiple lines when they exceed the container width
Creates a border around flex items
Wraps the container in a parent element
explanation: flex-wrap: wrap allows flex items to flow onto additional lines rather than shrinking to fit in one line when the container runs out of space.

question: What does "grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(200px, 1fr))" create?
options: A responsive grid that auto-fills as many 200px+ columns as fit
A grid that fills the viewport with 1fr columns
explanation: This creates a responsive grid where columns are at least 200px wide and expand to fill available space. auto-fill creates as many tracks as fit in the container.

question: What is the difference between "auto-fill" and "auto-fit" in CSS Grid?
options: auto-fill keeps empty tracks; auto-fit collapses empty tracks to 0
auto-fit creates more columns than auto-fill
auto-fill only works with fixed sizes
explanation: auto-fill creates as many tracks as fit and keeps empty ones. auto-fit collapses empty tracks to 0, causing remaining items to stretch and fill the space.

question: What does "grid-area" shorthand set?
options: The area of each grid cell in pixels
explanation: grid-area is shorthand for grid-row-start / grid-column-start / grid-row-end / grid-column-end, or it can reference a named grid area.

question: How do you create a grid layout with named template areas?
options: Using grid-template-areas with quoted strings defining area names
Named areas are not supported in CSS Grid
explanation: grid-template-areas uses quoted strings where each string represents a row and each word a cell. Repeating a name spans that area across cells.

question: What is the "subgrid" value in CSS Grid?
options: Allows a nested grid to inherit track sizing from its parent grid
Creates a smaller version of the parent grid
Splits each grid cell into sub-cells
explanation: subgrid allows a nested grid item to adopt the track sizing of its parent grid, enabling aligned layouts across nested components.

question: What is the difference between CSS transitions and animations?
options: Transitions animate between two states on trigger; animations can have multiple keyframes and run independently
Animations require JavaScript; transitions do not
They are identical but with different syntax
explanation: CSS transitions animate property changes between two states (triggered by :hover, class changes, etc.). CSS animations use @keyframes for complex, multi-step animations that can run automatically.

question: What does "transform: translate3d(0, 0, 0)" achieve?
options: Promotes the element to its own GPU compositing layer for better performance
Resets all transforms on the element
explanation: translate3d(0,0,0) is a common hack to force GPU acceleration by promoting the element to its own compositing layer, improving animation performance.

question: Which CSS properties can be animated performantly (without triggering layout)?
explanation: transform and opacity can be handled by the compositor thread without triggering layout or paint, making them the most performant properties to animate.

question: What is the "will-change" CSS property used for?
options: Hints to the browser about which properties will change, allowing optimization
Changes the element automatically based on viewport
Defines what properties will change on hover
explanation: will-change hints to the browser that specific properties will change soon, allowing it to set up optimizations like creating a compositing layer ahead of time.

question: What are CSS Container Queries?
options: Allow styling based on the size of a parent container rather than the viewport
explanation: Container queries (@container) allow component-level responsive design, styling elements based on their container size instead of the viewport.

question: What does the CSS ":has()" selector do?
options: Selects a parent element based on its children or descendants
Checks if an element has a specific attribute
Selects elements that have been visited
Tests if an element has any content
explanation: :has() is often called the "parent selector" - it selects elements based on what they contain. For example, div:has(> img) selects divs with a direct img child.

question: What is CSS nesting?
options: Writing CSS rules inside other rules to reflect HTML structure, reducing repetition
Nesting HTML elements inside each other
Importing CSS files inside other CSS files
explanation: Native CSS nesting allows writing child selectors inside parent rules (like Sass), reducing repetition: .card { .title { color: red; } }

question: What does the "@layer" CSS rule do?
options: Creates cascade layers to control the order and priority of style rules
Adds a visual layer effect to elements
explanation: @layer creates cascade layers that let authors control the cascade order of their styles, useful for managing specificity in large codebases and design systems.

question: What is the "clamp()" CSS function?
options: Sets a value that is clamped between a minimum and maximum: clamp(min, preferred, max)
Restricts an element to a fixed size
Clamps text to a specific number of lines
Limits the number of child elements
explanation: clamp(min, preferred, max) returns the preferred value if it falls between min and max, otherwise returns the boundary value. Great for responsive typography.

question: What is the CSS "aspect-ratio" property?
options: Sets a preferred aspect ratio for an element (e.g., 16/9)
Calculates the ratio of width to height automatically
Forces an image to a specific aspect ratio
explanation: The aspect-ratio property sets a preferred width-to-height ratio for an element. Combined with width or height, the other dimension is calculated automatically.

question: What does "accent-color" do in CSS?
options: Sets the accent color for form controls like checkboxes, radio buttons, and range inputs
Sets the highlight color for selected text
explanation: accent-color allows customizing the color of built-in form controls (checkboxes, radio buttons, progress bars, range inputs) without complex custom styling.

question: What is a "stacking context" in CSS?
options: A three-dimensional conceptualization of HTML elements along the z-axis that determines overlap order
The order in which CSS files are stacked
The nesting depth of HTML elements
explanation: A stacking context is formed by elements with certain properties (position + z-index, opacity < 1, transform, etc.) and determines how overlapping elements are rendered.

question: What is the difference between "overflow: hidden" and "overflow: clip"?
options: "clip" does not create a scroll container or stacking context; "hidden" does
"clip" only works on text; "hidden" works on all content
explanation: overflow: clip clips content without creating a scroll container. overflow: hidden also clips but creates a new block formatting context and scroll container.

question: What are CSS logical properties?
options: Properties that adapt to writing direction (e.g., margin-inline-start instead of margin-left)
Properties that use logical operators (AND, OR)
Properties that only apply when conditions are met
explanation: Logical properties (margin-inline, padding-block, etc.) adapt to the writing mode and direction, making layouts work correctly for RTL languages and vertical writing modes.

question: What is a CSS media query used for?
options: Applying different styles based on device characteristics like viewport width
Querying a database for style data
Selecting media elements like video and audio
Loading different HTML based on device
explanation: Media queries (@media) apply CSS rules conditionally based on device characteristics such as viewport width, height, orientation, color scheme, and more.

question: What does "prefers-color-scheme" media query detect?
options: Whether the user has requested a light or dark color theme at the OS level
The CSS color scheme of the current page
Whether colors are supported by the display
explanation: prefers-color-scheme detects the user's OS-level preference for light or dark mode, allowing websites to match the system theme.

question: What does "prefers-reduced-motion" media query detect?
options: Whether the user has requested reduced motion in their OS accessibility settings
The speed of the user's internet connection
The refresh rate of the display
explanation: prefers-reduced-motion detects if the user has enabled reduced motion in their OS settings, allowing developers to minimize or remove animations for accessibility.

question: What are CSS viewport units (vw, vh, vmin, vmax)?
options: Units relative to the viewport: vw = 1% width, vh = 1% height, vmin/vmax = smaller/larger dimension
Fixed pixel values for different viewports
Units that only work in mobile browsers
explanation: Viewport units are relative to the browser viewport: 1vw = 1% of viewport width, 1vh = 1% of viewport height. vmin and vmax use the smaller/larger of the two.

question: What is the "dvh" unit in CSS?
options: Dynamic viewport height that accounts for mobile browser UI changes (address bar showing/hiding)
explanation: dvh (dynamic viewport height) changes as the browser UI appears/disappears on mobile, unlike vh which is based on the largest possible viewport.

question: What does "font-display: swap" do in a @font-face rule?
options: Shows fallback text immediately, then swaps to the custom font when loaded
Displays text only after the font loads
explanation: font-display: swap shows text immediately using a fallback font, then "swaps" to the custom font once it downloads, preventing invisible text (FOIT).

question: What is the "text-wrap: balance" CSS property?
options: Distributes text more evenly across lines in headings for a visually balanced appearance
explanation: text-wrap: balance adjusts line breaks so text lines are more even in length, creating more visually appealing headings and short text blocks.

question: What is "ch" unit in CSS?
options: Width of the "0" (zero) character in the current font
explanation: The "ch" unit represents the advance measure (width) of the "0" glyph in the element's current font. Useful for setting optimal reading line lengths.

question: What is the difference between rgb(), hsl(), and oklch() in CSS?
options: rgb uses red-green-blue, hsl uses hue-saturation-lightness, oklch uses lightness-chroma-hue in a perceptually uniform space
oklch is deprecated in favor of rgb
hsl only works in dark mode
explanation: rgb() uses additive color mixing, hsl() uses a more intuitive color model, and oklch() provides perceptually uniform colors where equal numeric changes produce equal visual changes.

question: What does "color-scheme: light dark" do?
options: Tells the browser the page supports both light and dark color schemes, adjusting built-in UI accordingly
Changes the page colors based on time of day
explanation: color-scheme: light dark informs the browser that both schemes are supported. The browser then adjusts form controls, scrollbars, and system colors accordingly.

question: What are CSS conic-gradient() functions used for?
options: Creating gradients that rotate around a center point (like pie charts)
explanation: conic-gradient() creates gradients with color transitions rotated around a center point, useful for pie charts, color wheels, and decorative effects.

question: What is the difference between ::before and :before in CSS?
options: :: is the correct CSS3 syntax for pseudo-elements; : is the CSS2 legacy syntax (both work)
:: is for pseudo-classes; : is for pseudo-elements
explanation: CSS3 introduced :: for pseudo-elements to distinguish them from pseudo-classes (:). Both ::before and :before work, but :: is the correct modern syntax.

question: What does the ::placeholder pseudo-element style?
options: The placeholder text shown in form inputs before user types
explanation: ::placeholder styles the placeholder text in <input> and <textarea> elements. It has limited styleable properties (color, font, text-decoration, etc.).

question: What does the :focus-visible pseudo-class do?
options: Applies styles only when focus is visible to the user (keyboard navigation), not on mouse clicks
Makes focused elements visible on screen
Shows a visible indicator on all focused elements
explanation: :focus-visible matches elements that receive focus via keyboard navigation but not via mouse click, allowing you to show focus rings only when they are helpful.

question: What is the :where() pseudo-class function used for?
options: Creates a selector list with zero specificity, useful for easily overridable defaults
explanation: :where() works like :is() for grouping selectors, but has zero specificity, making it ideal for creating low-priority default styles in libraries.

question: What is the :is() pseudo-class function?
options: Groups selectors and takes on the highest specificity of its arguments
Tests if a value is valid
explanation: :is() takes a selector list and matches elements matching any selector in the list. Its specificity equals the most specific argument.

Fades out an element while sliding it down
Scales an element from 0 to full size

question: In the CSS box model, what is the default value of the box-sizing property?

explanation: content-box is the standard default where width and height apply only to the content area.

question: What occurs during CSS margin collapsing?

Adjacent vertical margins of block-level elements combine into a single margin

Negative margins are ignored by the browser rendering engine

question: Which condition prevents vertical margin collapsing between parent and child elements?

Setting display: inline on the parent element
Adding a 1px border or padding to the parent element
Applying font-size: 0 to the parent container
hint: A physical barrier stops margin collapsing.
explanation: Padding or borders on the parent separate the margins, preventing them from collapsing.

question: What is the key difference between outline and border in CSS?
options: Borders do not support rounded corners with border-radius
Borders cannot be styled with dashed or dotted lines
Outlines can only be rendered with solid black color
Outlines do not take up space in the document layout
explanation: An outline is drawn outside the element's border and does not affect page layout or element dimensions.

It forces the viewport to render in 16:9 widescreen format
It scales the font-size proportionately to 16px and 9px
It crops background images to standard 16:9 video boundaries

explanation: The aspect-ratio property sets a preferred aspect ratio for the box, which is used in auto sizes calculations.

question: How do negative margins behave in CSS when applied as 'margin-left: -20px'?

The element creates a 20px gap to its right sibling
The browser ignores the negative value and applies 0px
The element shrinks its width by 20 pixels
explanation: Negative margins pull the element in that direction or pull subsequent siblings closer.

question: Which CSS selector has the highest specificity?

explanation: Inline styles have a specificity weight of (1, 0, 0, 0), beating IDs (0, 1, 0, 0).

question: What is the specificity value of the selector 'div.container ul li.active a'?

question: How does the specificity of the CSS ':where()' pseudo-class compare to ':is()'?

:where() always has 0 specificity, whereas :is() takes the specificity of its most specific argument
explanation: :where() resets specificity to zero, making it ideal for resets and CSS libraries.

question: What does the ':has()' relational pseudo-class selector match?

Elements with at least one custom data-attribute

question: Which pseudo-class selector targets an input element when its value passes HTML validation?

question: What does the selector 'a[href^="https"]' target in CSS?

All paragraph descendants inside a div at any nesting level
Paragraph elements immediately following a div sibling
Direct paragraph children of a div element
explanation: The child combinator (>) selects elements that are immediate direct children of the specified parent.

question: What is the difference between ':nth-child(2)' and ':nth-of-type(2)'?
options: :nth-of-type(2) only counts siblings that share the same tag name
They are identical aliases in CSS3
explanation: :nth-of-type filters by element type first before counting, while :nth-child counts all siblings regardless of type.

question: Which property sets the main axis direction in a Flexbox container?
explanation: flex-direction sets the direction of the flex container's main axis (row, column, row-reverse, column-reverse).

question: What is the default value of 'flex-direction' on a flex container?
explanation: The initial default flex-direction is 'row', laying items out horizontally from left to right in LTR.

question: Which CSS Flexbox property aligns items along the cross axis?
explanation: align-items specifies the default alignment for items along the cross axis inside a flex line.

question: What is the difference between 'align-items' and 'align-content' in Flexbox?
options: 'align-content' aligns text inside individual flex items
'align-content' aligns multi-line flex tracks when extra cross-axis space exists
explanation: align-content only takes effect when there is extra space on the cross axis and flex-wrap is set to wrap/wrap-reverse.

question: What does the shorthand 'flex: 1' expand to in standard CSS?
explanation: The flex: 1 shorthand sets flex-grow to 1, flex-shrink to 1, and flex-basis to 0%.

question: What does 'justify-content: space-between' do in a flex container?
options: Distributes items with equal space around each item including ends
Distributes items evenly; first item is flush at start, last item flush at end
Centers all flex items with equal margins on both sides
Packs items tightly toward the end of the main axis
explanation: space-between puts the first item at the start edge, last item at the end edge, and equal spacing in between.

question: What is the default value of 'flex-shrink' on a flex item?
explanation: By default, flex items have flex-shrink: 1, allowing them to shrink to prevent overflowing the container.

question: Which property on a flex item overrides the container's 'align-items' setting?
explanation: align-self allows individual flex items to override the container's align-items property.

question: Why does 'justify-self' have no effect on items in a Flexbox container?
options: The main axis is controlled as a collective group by the container via justify-content
Flexbox does not support self-alignment on any axis
justify-self is deprecated in CSS3 in favor of margin-inline
Flex items always span 100% width of the container
hint: Auto margins achieve self-alignment on main axis.
explanation: In Flexbox, items share space on the main axis together; auto margins can be used instead of justify-self.

question: Which CSS display value defines a grid container?
explanation: Setting display: grid or display: inline-grid establishes a new grid formatting context.

question: What does the 'fr' unit represent in CSS Grid?
options: A frame rate unit for CSS animations
A fixed ratio calculated from screen dpi
A fraction of the available space inside the grid container
A font-relative scaling factor matching em
explanation: The fr unit represents a fraction of the leftover space in the grid container after non-flexible items are sized.

question: What is the difference between 'auto-fill' and 'auto-fit' in 'repeat()'?
options: 'auto-fill' collapses empty tracks while 'auto-fit' preserves them
'auto-fit' collapses empty tracks to 0px, allowing filled tracks to stretch
'auto-fit' only works with fixed pixel widths
'auto-fill' prevents items from wrapping onto new rows
explanation: auto-fit expands active tracks to take up the space of any empty phantom tracks, while auto-fill keeps empty tracks reserved.

question: Which CSS property defines column sizes in a Grid layout?
explanation: grid-template-columns defines the line names and track sizing functions of the grid columns.

question: What does 'grid-column: 1 / -1' achieve on a grid item?
options: The item takes the full height of the first row
The item is placed on the second-to-last column
The item is hidden from the grid rendering tree
The item spans across all columns from the first line to the last line
explanation: -1 refers to the last grid line, so 1 / -1 makes the item span the entire width of explicit grid columns.

question: What is the purpose of 'minmax(200px, 1fr)' in CSS Grid?
options: The track will be at least 200px wide, and expand up to 1 fraction of free space
The track toggles between 200px on mobile and 1fr on desktop
The track cannot exceed 200px under any screen size
The track reserves 200px padding before assigning 1fr
explanation: minmax() defines a size range greater than or equal to min and less than or equal to max.

question: Which property sets the spacing between both rows and columns in CSS Grid?
explanation: The gap shorthand (formerly grid-gap) sets the gutters between grid rows and columns.

question: What does 'subgrid' allow a nested grid element to do?
options: Automatically convert Flexbox children into grid cells
Create a separate 3D rendering context for children
Inherit its track sizing and grid lines from the parent grid
Duplicate the HTML markup of the parent container
explanation: display: grid; grid-template-columns: subgrid allows the child grid to align its own children directly to the parent's tracks.

question: Which CSS position value positions an element relative to the viewport?
explanation: position: fixed places the element relative to the initial viewport, remaining in place during scrolling.

question: What is the default value of the CSS 'position' property?
explanation: position: static is the default; elements render in the normal document flow and ignore top, right, bottom, left.

question: An element has 'position: absolute'. What is it positioned relative to?
options: Its closest ancestor that has a position other than static
Its direct parent element regardless of positioning
The center of the active browser viewport
explanation: position: absolute positions relative to the nearest positioned ancestor (position relative, absolute, fixed, or sticky).

question: What is required for 'position: sticky' to stick during scrolling?
options: The element must have display: flex declared
The parent container must have overflow: hidden
At least one threshold property like 'top', 'bottom', 'left', or 'right' must be set
z-index must be set to 9999 or higher
explanation: Sticky positioning requires a directional offset (e.g., top: 0) to know where to anchor.

question: Which of the following creates a new stacking context in CSS?
explanation: Opacity < 1, transforms, filters, and will-change create a new stacking context independent of z-index.

question: Why might 'z-index: 9999' fail to place an element above another element?
options: The browser disables z-index on desktop screens
z-index only accepts values between 0 and 100
z-index requires display: table to function
The element is inside a lower stacking context than the competing element
explanation: z-index only applies within its own stacking context; a child cannot escape a parent's lower stacking level.

question: What does '1rem' represent in CSS?
options: The font size of the root (<html>) element
The font size of the immediate parent element
A fixed size equal to 12 points
explanation: rem stands for 'root em', which is relative to the font-size of the root element (usually 16px by default).

question: What is the difference between unitless line-height (e.g. 1.5) and percentage line-height (150%)?
options: Percentage line-height adapts to viewport changes while unitless does not
Unitless line-height allows child elements to inherit the ratio and compute based on their own font-size
Unitless line-height is deprecated in CSS3
There is no difference in rendering or inheritance
explanation: With unitless line-height, children inherit the multiplier; with percentages, the computed pixel value is inherited.

question: What does 'font-display: swap' do in a @font-face declaration?
options: Swaps between serif and sans-serif depending on system theme
Hides the text completely until the custom font downloads
Displays a fallback font immediately until the custom web font finishes loading
Forces the browser to block page rendering until font loads
explanation: swap gives the font face an extremely small block period and an infinite swap period, preventing invisible text (FOIT).

question: Which CSS property controls letter spacing between characters?
explanation: letter-spacing sets the horizontal spacing behavior between text characters.

question: What does the CSS property 'text-overflow: ellipsis' require to display '...'?
options: overflow: hidden, white-space: nowrap, and a bounded width
explanation: Ellipsis requires overflow: hidden and white-space: nowrap so that text overflows a constrained container.

question: How do you define a global CSS Custom Property (variable)?
explanation: CSS variables are declared with a double hyphen prefix (--) and commonly scoped to :root for global access.

question: How do you access a CSS custom property named '--brand-color'?
explanation: The var() function retrieves the value of a custom property.

question: What is the purpose of the second argument in 'var(--accent, #3b82f6)'?
options: It sets the dark-mode color override
It sets the hover state color
It defines a CSS transition duration
It provides a fallback value if the custom property is not defined
explanation: The second parameter in var() is a fallback value used if the variable is invalid or undefined.

question: What does 'clamp(1rem, 2.5vw, 2rem)' evaluate to?
options: A random value clamped to browser DPI
An average of the three values
1rem on mobile and 2rem on desktop only
A value that scales with viewport width between a minimum of 1rem and a maximum of 2rem
explanation: clamp(MIN, VAL, MAX) clamps a value between an upper and lower bound.

question: What does the '@container' rule enable in modern CSS?
options: Styles based on the size of an ancestor container rather than the viewport
Styles applied only inside iframe containers
Docker container detection in server-side CSS
explanation: Container queries allow styling components based on the dimensions of their parent container.

question: What is the purpose of 'color-scheme: dark light' in CSS?
options: Forces the screen to invert all image colors
Informs the browser that the element supports both dark and light system themes
Applies a CSS filter to simulate night vision
explanation: color-scheme allows an element to indicate which color schemes it can comfortably render with system form controls.

question: Which CSS property specifies how long an animation takes to complete one cycle?
explanation: animation-duration sets the length of time that an animation takes to complete one cycle.

question: What does 'animation-fill-mode: forwards' do?
options: The animation starts immediately without respecting animation-delay
The animation plays backward upon reaching the end
The element retains the styles computed by the last keyframe after the animation finishes
explanation: forwards ensures the element retains the style values calculated in the final keyframe.

question: What is the purpose of the 'will-change' property in CSS?
options: Hints to the browser what properties will animate so it can optimize rendering upfront
Forces the browser to reload stylesheets every 5 seconds
Enables CSS variables in older legacy browsers
explanation: will-change informs the browser about planned changes so it can set up ahead-of-time GPU optimizations.

question: Which CSS rule defines the intermediate steps in an animation sequence?
explanation: The @keyframes at-rule defines keyframes that control intermediate steps in a CSS animation sequence.

question: Which transition-timing-function produces an animation with constant speed?
explanation: linear maintains the exact same speed from beginning to end without acceleration.

question: Which CSS properties are most performant to animate without triggering layout or paint?
explanation: transform and opacity can be composited directly on the GPU without triggering reflow (layout) or repaint.

question: What is a 'mobile-first' approach in CSS development?
options: Writing base styles for small screens and using 'min-width' media queries for larger displays
Developing native mobile apps using React Native before web
Disabling desktop layouts completely on mobile devices
Writing styles using max-width queries starting from 4K displays
explanation: Mobile-first styles default to mobile layouts and add progressive enhancements using min-width.

question: Which media query targets devices whose users prefer reduced motion?
explanation: prefers-reduced-motion detects if the user has requested the system minimize animations.

question: What does the viewport unit 'dvh' represent in CSS?
options: Display Viewport Height for desktop monitors
Dynamic Viewport Height, which adapts to mobile browser interface bars showing or hiding
Device Virtual Height calculated before CSS loads
explanation: dvh dynamically adjusts as mobile URL bars and toolbars expand and collapse during scrolling.

question: What do the values in 'hsl(210, 50%, 60%)' represent?
explanation: HSL stands for Hue (0-360 on the color wheel), Saturation (0-100%), and Lightness (0-100%).

question: Why is the 'oklch' color space increasingly preferred in modern CSS?
options: It is the only color format supported in web workers
It can only display monochromatic shades of gray
It uses hexadecimal notation for faster parsing
It is perceptually uniform, meaning equal adjustments produce visually consistent brightness changes
explanation: OKLCH matches human eye perception uniformly across different hues.

question: Which pseudo-element is used to insert generated content before an element's content?
explanation: The ::before pseudo-element creates a pseudo-element that is the first child of the selected element, styled using the content property.

question: What CSS property is mandatory for '::before' and '::after' pseudo-elements to render?
explanation: Without the content property (even content: ''), pseudo-elements will not be generated.

question: What is the difference between single colon (:hover) and double colon (::after) in modern CSS?
options: Single colon only applies to links
Double colon is deprecated in CSS3
Single colon denotes a pseudo-class (state), while double colon denotes a pseudo-element (part of DOM)
explanation: CSS3 introduced the double-colon syntax to distinguish pseudo-elements from pseudo-classes.

question: Which pseudo-element styles the portion of a document selected and highlighted by the user?
explanation: The ::selection pseudo-element applies styles to the part of a document that has been highlighted by the user.

question: Which pseudo-element styles the placeholder text inside an input field?
explanation: The ::placeholder pseudo-element represents the placeholder text in an <input> or <textarea> element.

question: What happens to width and height properties when applied to a purely 'inline' element like <span>?
options: They are ignored by the browser
They cause the element to convert to display: block
They produce a CSS syntax error
explanation: Width and height do not apply to non-replaced inline elements.

question: How does 'display: inline-block' differ from 'display: inline'?
options: inline-block forces a line break before and after the element
inline-block respects width and height while flowing inline with surrounding text
inline-block cannot have padding or margins
inline-block is not supported in modern browsers
explanation: inline-block allows setting explicit dimensions while maintaining horizontal flow.

question: What does 'display: contents' do to an element?
options: Converts the element into a shadow DOM container
Hides the element and all its children completely from view
The element itself does not generate boxes, but its children render as direct children of the parent
Forces all text inside the element to wrap
explanation: display: contents removes the wrapper box from the layout tree while keeping its children intact.

question: What is the key visual difference between 'display: none' and 'visibility: hidden'?
options: There is no difference between them
'visibility: hidden' removes the element from DOM tree entirely
'display: none' can still be clicked by the user
'display: none' removes the element from document flow, while 'visibility: hidden' leaves empty space
explanation: display: none collapses space; visibility: hidden hides pixels while retaining layout footprint.

question: Which CSS property prevents a background image from repeating across a container?
explanation: background-repeat: no-repeat ensures the image renders only once.

question: What does 'background-size: cover' do?
options: Stretches the image to fit without maintaining aspect ratio
Scales the image to completely cover the container, potentially clipping edges
Scales the image so the entire image is visible without clipping
Tiles the image until the background is filled
explanation: cover scales proportionately so no background area is left uncovered, cropping if ratios differ.

question: What does 'background-size: contain' do?
options: Expands the container to match original image dimensions
Stretches the image to fill 100% width and 100% height
Scales the image as large as possible without cropping any part of the image
explanation: contain ensures the entire image fits inside the box, potentially leaving empty background margins.

question: What is the difference between 'filter: blur()' and 'backdrop-filter: blur()'?
options: 'backdrop-filter' blurs the text inside the element
'backdrop-filter' blurs what is visible behind the element through transparency
explanation: backdrop-filter applies graphical effects to the area behind an element with partial opacity.

question: Which CSS property transforms text to all uppercase characters?
explanation: text-transform controls capitalization of text without changing source HTML.

question: What is the function of 'white-space: nowrap' in CSS?
options: Collapses all spaces into a single hyphen
Prevents text from automatically wrapping onto a new line
Forces every word onto its own line
Converts all spaces into non-breaking spaces in HTML
explanation: white-space: nowrap suppresses line breaks within the element.

question: What does 'overflow-wrap: break-word' (or 'word-break: break-word') accomplish?
options: Hides long words that overflow the container
Hyphenates every word automatically using a dictionary
Allows long, unbreakable words to break and wrap onto a new line if necessary
Scales down font size for long words
explanation: overflow-wrap: break-word breaks words at arbitrary points to prevent layout overflow.

question: Which CSS function performs mathematical calculations like addition and multiplication?
explanation: calc() allows mathematical calculations for CSS property values mixing different units.

question: Can you mix different units like percentages and pixels inside 'calc()'?
options: No, all units must match exactly
Only if both units are relative units
explanation: calc() dynamically evaluates mixed units at layout time.

question: What does the 'min()' CSS function return?
options: The smallest value among the provided arguments
The average of the supplied values
The minimum font size supported by browser
The initial value before stylesheets loaded
explanation: min() selects the smallest value from a comma-separated list of expressions.

question: What does the 'max()' CSS function return?
options: The largest value among the provided arguments
The largest font size possible in CSS
The absolute value of negative numbers
explanation: max() selects the largest value from a comma-separated list of expressions.

question: What does the sibling combinator '~' (e.g. 'h2 ~ p') select?
options: All p elements nested inside h2
Only the immediately adjacent p element after h2
All p elements that follow an h2 element as siblings
explanation: The general sibling combinator (~) selects all subsequent siblings matching the right operand.

question: What does the adjacent sibling combinator '+' (e.g. 'h2 + p') select?
options: The preceding sibling element before h2
All sibling paragraphs in the entire document
The first paragraph inside the h2 tag
The immediately following p sibling after an h2 element
explanation: The adjacent sibling combinator (+) selects the element directly following the first element.

question: Which pseudo-class targets an element when the user hovers over it with a pointing device?
explanation: The :hover pseudo-class matches when the user interacts with an element with a pointer device.

question: Which pseudo-class targets an element when it receives keyboard or mouse focus?
explanation: The :focus pseudo-class represents an element that has received focus, such as via Tab key.

question: What is the difference between ':focus' and ':focus-visible'?
options: ':focus-visible' is applied to every element simultaneously
':focus' is only triggered on touch devices
':focus-visible' only shows focus indicators when keyboard navigation is used
':focus' cannot be styled with custom outlines
explanation: :focus-visible avoids jarring focus rings for mouse clicks while keeping them for keyboard users.

question: Which pseudo-class selects an element that is the target of the URL's fragment identifier?
explanation: The :target pseudo-class represents a unique element with an id matching the URL fragment.

question: Which pseudo-class matches an empty element with no children or text nodes?
explanation: The :empty pseudo-class represents any element that has no children at all (including text).

question: What does ':not(.active)' do in CSS?
options: Selects all elements that do not have the 'active' class
Removes the active class from DOM elements
Sets opacity to zero for inactive items
explanation: The negation pseudo-class :not() represents elements that do not match a list of selectors.

question: Which CSS property delays the start of an animation or transition?
explanation: animation-delay defines the duration to wait before starting execution.

question: What does 'animation-iteration-count: infinite' do?
options: Freezes the animation on its first frame
Loops the animation 1,000 times then stops
Makes the animation repeat indefinitely without stopping
explanation: infinite makes the keyframe sequence loop continuously.

question: What does 'animation-direction: alternate' do?
options: Rotates the element 180 degrees on each loop
Plays the animation forward on odd cycles and backward on even cycles
explanation: alternate causes the animation to reverse direction every cycle.

question: What does 'animation-play-state: paused' accomplish?
options: Temporarily halts an active CSS animation at its current frame
Resets the animation back to frame 0%
Hides the animating element from layout
explanation: animation-play-state allows pausing and resuming animations dynamically.

question: What does 'scroll-snap-type: y mandatory' on a scroll container do?
options: Forces the scroll position to snap to snap points along the vertical axis
Smoothly auto-scrolls to the bottom of the page
explanation: scroll-snap-type enforces snap points when scrolling ends.

question: What property is applied to child items inside a scroll-snap container?
explanation: scroll-snap-align defines where child items snap within the viewport.

question: What does 'overscroll-behavior: contain' prevent?
options: Locks zoom levels on touch devices
Prevents images from loading outside the viewport
Prevents scroll chaining (rubber-banding) to parent containers when scroll boundary is reached
explanation: overscroll-behavior sets what a browser does when reaching the boundary of a scrolling area.

question: What does 'user-select: none' do in CSS?
options: Prevents users from selecting and highlighting text within the element
Hides the cursor arrow on hover
explanation: user-select: none prevents text selection for UI elements like buttons and chips.

question: Which CSS property changes the mouse pointer appearance when hovering over an element?
explanation: cursor defines the mouse cursor to be displayed when pointing over an element (e.g. pointer, not-allowed).

question: What does 'pointer-events: none' do on an HTML element?
options: Hides the mouse cursor while hovering
Makes the element completely transparent to click, hover, and touch events
explanation: pointer-events: none makes the element ignore pointer interactions, passing them to elements underneath.

question: What does the CSS keyword 'inherit' do when assigned to a property?
options: Deletes the property from the stylesheet
Resets the property to browser user-agent default
Forces the property to take the computed value of its parent element
Copies the style from the root <html> element
explanation: inherit causes the element to take the computed value of the property from its parent.

question: What does the CSS keyword 'initial' do?
options: Reverts to the author stylesheet value
Inherits the value from its parent element
Uses the browser default stylesheet style
Sets the property to its initial value as defined in the official CSS specification
explanation: initial resets a property to its default value according to the W3C spec (not user agent default).

question: What does the CSS keyword 'unset' do?
options: Inherits the value if property naturally inherits, otherwise acts like initial
Deletes the element from the DOM
explanation: unset acts like inherit for inherited properties and initial for non-inherited properties.

question: What does the CSS keyword 'revert' do?
options: Sets the property to initial specification value
Reverts the property value to the browser's default user-agent stylesheet style
Deletes all inline styles from HTML
explanation: revert resets cascade to the user-agent or user stylesheet layer.

question: How does '!important' affect CSS specificity?
options: Converts the rule into an inline style attribute
Multiplies the selector specificity score by 10
Overrides normal cascade and specificity rules for that declaration
explanation: !important causes a declaration to override standard cascade order and selector specificity.

question: Why does an image inside a flex container sometimes stretch unexpectedly along the cross axis?
options: flex-grow is set to 1 by default on images
Flex containers always upscale raster images
explanation: align-items: stretch causes items without explicit cross-axis sizes to fill the container height.

question: How can you horizontally and vertically center a child in Flexbox with 2 lines of CSS?
options: display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center;
display: flex; float: center; margin: auto;
explanation: justify-content centers along the main axis and align-items centers along the cross axis.

question: What happens if a flex item has 'margin: auto' applied in a flex container?
options: It absorbs all remaining free space in that direction, centering or pushing the item
It disables flex-grow on all items
It aligns the item to the start edge
explanation: In Flexbox, auto margins consume all available extra space along that axis.

question: What is the difference between an explicit grid and an implicit grid?
options: The explicit grid is created by JavaScript, implicit by CSS
The implicit grid is created automatically when items are positioned outside explicit tracks
The implicit grid cannot use the gap property
Explicit grids only support pixel sizing
explanation: Tracks defined by grid-template-* are explicit; items placed beyond create implicit tracks sized by grid-auto-*.

question: Which property controls the size of automatically created rows in an implicit grid?
explanation: grid-auto-rows specifies the size of an implicitly-created grid row track.

question: What does 'grid-auto-flow: dense' do?
options: Forces all grid items to have identical height
Fills in earlier holes in the grid if smaller items appear later in the source order
explanation: dense attempts to pack items tightly into empty gaps earlier in the grid layout.

question: How do you place an item in grid column 2, row 3?
explanation: grid-column and grid-row specify placement line or span.

question: Which CSS transform function moves an element horizontally and vertically?
explanation: translate(x, y) moves an element along the X and Y axes.

question: Which CSS transform function rotates an element around a fixed point?
explanation: rotate() rotates an element around its transform-origin by a specified angle.

question: What does 'transform-origin: center center' define?
options: The center of the browser viewport
The alignment of text inside the transformed box
The pivot point around which transforms like rotate and scale are applied
explanation: transform-origin sets the origin point for an element's transformations (defaults to 50% 50%).

question: What is required to render genuine 3D transformed child elements inside a parent?
options: transform-style: preserve-3d on the parent element
explanation: transform-style: preserve-3d ensures children exist in shared 3D space rather than being flattened.

question: What does the 'perspective' property in CSS do?
options: Determines the distance between the z=0 plane and the viewer for 3D transforms
Sets the opacity gradient for depth
explanation: perspective gives depth to 3D-positioned elements by simulating perspective foreshortening.

question: How do you make flex items wrap onto multiple lines when container space is exceeded?
explanation: flex-wrap: wrap allows flex items to wrap onto multiple lines as needed.

question: Which shorthand property combines 'flex-direction' and 'flex-wrap' in CSS?
explanation: flex-flow is a shorthand for flex-direction and flex-wrap.

question: How do you center an item both horizontally and vertically inside a grid container?
explanation: place-items: center is a shorthand for align-items: center and justify-items: center.

question: Which property sets alignment of items along the inline axis within their grid areas?
explanation: justify-items aligns grid items along the inline (row) axis inside their grid areas.

question: Which property sets alignment of items along the block axis within their grid areas?
explanation: align-items aligns grid items along the block (column) axis inside their grid areas.

question: What does 'grid-template-areas' allow you to do in CSS Grid?
options: Set automatic background colors for rows
Define SVG clipping paths for grid cells
Name visual rectangular areas in the grid using strings of identifiers
explanation: grid-template-areas assigns named template areas to layout sections visually.

question: What CSS property creates rounded corners on an element's border?
explanation: border-radius rounds the corners of an element's outer border edge.

question: What property adds drop shadows to box elements in CSS?
explanation: box-shadow adds shadow effects around an element's frame.

question: What does the 'inset' keyword do in a 'box-shadow' declaration?
options: Draws the shadow inside the frame of the element
Centers the shadow evenly on all sides
explanation: inset places the shadow inside the border of the box.

question: What CSS property clips an element's content to a basic shape like circle or polygon?
explanation: clip-path creates a clipping region that sets what part of an element is visible.

question: Which property styles text in italics?
explanation: font-style specifies whether text is rendered in normal, italic, or oblique face.

question: Which CSS property specifies the boldness or weight of a font?
explanation: font-weight sets how thick or thin characters in text should be displayed.

question: Which CSS property adds an underline, overline, or line-through to text?
explanation: text-decoration sets text decoration lines and styles.

question: What does 'text-align: justify' do?
options: Spaces text so that both left and right edges align with the container margins
Aligns text strictly to the right margin
Scales the font to fill the container height
explanation: justify adjusts letter and word spacing so lines align on both margins.

question: What is the alpha channel in an 'rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.5)' color declaration?
options: The opacity / transparency level from 0 (transparent) to 1 (opaque)
explanation: Alpha specifies the opacity level of the color.

question: Which CSS property sets the transparency level of an entire element including its children?
explanation: opacity applies to the whole element and all its children uniformly.

question: What CSS at-rule is used to apply styles conditionally based on media features?
explanation: @media specifies rules conditional on media type and features.

question: Which media query feature checks if the screen orientation is taller than it is wide?
explanation: orientation: portrait tests whether height is greater than or equal to width.

question: What does '100vw' represent in CSS?
options: 100% of the viewport width including the scrollbar
explanation: vw represents 1% of the viewport width.

question: What does '100vh' represent in CSS?
explanation: vh represents 1% of the viewport height.

question: What does 'accent-color' in CSS style?
options: The primary brand color of CSS variables
The color of anchor links on hover
The title bar color in the browser
The accent color for native form elements like checkboxes, radios, and progress bars
explanation: accent-color specifies the accent color for user-interface controls generated by the browser.

question: What does 'caret-color' specify in CSS?
options: The color of text selection highlights
The color of breadcrumb arrow icons
The color of drop-down menu arrows
The color of the insertion cursor in text inputs and editable areas
explanation: caret-color sets the color of the text insertion cursor (caret).

question: What does 'image-rendering: pixelated' do?
options: Uses nearest-neighbor scaling so pixel art remains crisp when upscaled
Blurs the image using bicubic filtering
Compresses image file size in memory
explanation: pixelated preserves sharp edges on pixel graphics when scaled up.

question: What does 'writing-mode: vertical-rl' do in CSS?
options: Flows text vertically from top to bottom, with lines progressing from right to left
explanation: writing-mode sets whether lines of text are laid out horizontally or vertically.

question: What does 'mix-blend-mode: multiply' do in CSS?
options: Duplicates the element across the grid
Blends an element's content with the content of the elements behind it
explanation: mix-blend-mode sets how an element's content blends with its background.

question: What does the ':only-child' pseudo-class select?
options: An element with only one child of its own
An element that has no siblings at all inside its parent
explanation: The :only-child pseudo-class represents an element that has no siblings.

question: What does the ':root' pseudo-class select in an HTML document?
explanation: In HTML, :root represents the <html> element and has higher specificity than the html type selector.

question: What does ':checked' pseudo-class match in forms?
options: Radio buttons, checkboxes, and option elements that are checked or selected
Submit buttons that have been clicked
explanation: :checked matches radio buttons and checkboxes that are toggled on, or selected options in a select.

question: What does ':disabled' pseudo-class match?
options: Form elements that have the 'disabled' attribute applied
explanation: :disabled matches elements that cannot be activated or accept focus.

question: What does ':read-only' pseudo-class match?
options: Form elements that are not editable by the user
explanation: :read-only represents an element that is not editable by the user.

question: What does ':first-of-type' select?
options: The first sibling of its element type in a parent container
The very first child of any type
The first class listed in the class attribute
The element with the lowest z-index
explanation: :first-of-type represents the first element of its type among its group of sibling elements.

question: What does ':last-of-type' select?
options: The last sibling of its element type in a parent container
The last child element of any type
The element with the highest DOM index
explanation: :last-of-type represents the last element of its type among its group of siblings.

question: What does the selector '[disabled]' match?
options: Any element with a 'disabled' attribute regardless of its value
explanation: An attribute presence selector [attr] matches elements that have that attribute.

question: Which property sets the minimum width an element can shrink to?
explanation: min-width prevents the used value of the width property from becoming smaller than specified.

question: Which property sets the maximum width an element can expand to?
explanation: max-width prevents the used value of width from becoming larger than specified.

question: Which property sets the minimum height an element can shrink to?
explanation: min-height prevents the height property from becoming smaller than specified.

question: Which property sets the maximum height an element can reach?
explanation: max-height prevents the used value of height from becoming larger than specified.

question: What does 'overflow: auto' do when an element's content exceeds its box?
options: Always displays permanent scrollbars even if empty
Displays scrollbars only when the content actually overflows
explanation: auto tells the browser to provide scroll mechanisms only if content overflows.

question: What does 'overflow: scroll' do?
options: Only scrolls when triggered by JavaScript
Always displays scrollbars regardless of whether content overflows
explanation: overflow: scroll always shows scrollbars on platforms that support them, preventing layout shifts.

question: What does 'overflow: hidden' do?
options: Clips content that extends beyond the element's padding box
Expands the element to fit all content
Shows a modal popup for clipped content
explanation: overflow: hidden clips any content that overflows the element's boundaries.

question: What does 'font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums' do?
options: Renders numbers with equal character widths so columns of figures align cleanly
Rounds decimals to the nearest whole integer
explanation: tabular-nums enables monospaced figures in proportional fonts, perfect for timers and tables.

question: What does 'text-transform: capitalize' do?
options: Converts the entire string to all caps
Capitalizes the first character of each word in the text
Only capitalizes the very first letter of the paragraph
explanation: capitalize transforms the first letter of each word to uppercase.

question: What does 'text-shadow: 2px 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.5)' do?
options: Adds an inner box shadow behind the paragraph
Creates a 4px border around every text character
Adds a shadow to text with 2px horizontal offset, 2px vertical offset, and 4px blur radius
explanation: text-shadow applies one or more shadows to text content.

question: What does 'animation-fill-mode: backwards' do?
options: Retains styles after the animation finishes
Plays the animation from end to start
Disables animation on back button navigation
Applies the styles defined in the first keyframe (0%) during the animation-delay period
explanation: backwards applies the style from the initial keyframe during the delay period before playback starts.

question: What does 'animation-fill-mode: both' do?
options: Applies the animation styles both during the delay (0%) and after completion (100%)
Plays the animation simultaneously forward and backward
Applies the animation to both parent and child elements
Runs two keyframe rules in parallel
explanation: both applies both backwards and forwards rules.

question: What does '@media (hover: hover)' detect?
options: Whether the user is currently hovering over an element
Whether the primary input mechanism can hover over elements (e.g. mouse pointer)
Whether hover animations are supported by the GPU
explanation: hover: hover tests if the primary pointing device can hover over page elements.

question: What does '@media (pointer: coarse)' detect?
options: Whether the screen resolution is low quality
Whether the user is using a precision high-DPI gaming mouse
Whether the primary input device is of limited accuracy (such as a touch screen finger)
Whether the device has a physical trackpad
explanation: pointer: coarse indicates touch devices with less precision than mice.

question: What does the ':user-valid' pseudo-class represent in modern form styling?
options: An input that passed validation before page load
An input validated by a remote server API
A password input with biometric authentication
An input whose value is valid, but only after the user has interacted with it
explanation: :user-valid matches valid inputs only after user interaction, preventing premature error states.

question: What does the ':user-invalid' pseudo-class represent?
options: An input whose value is invalid, but only after the user has attempted interaction
An input disabled by the server
An input with an invalid type attribute
explanation: :user-invalid prevents showing aggressive validation errors before the user finishes typing.

question: What does 'isolation: isolate' do in CSS?
options: Isolates the element in an iframe sandbox
Creates a new stacking context without requiring z-index or opacity hacks
explanation: isolation: isolate defines whether an element must create a new stacking context.

question: Which property sets whether an element displays as a block or inline box?
explanation: display specifies the box's inner and outer display types.

question: Which property sets the distance between borders of adjacent cells in a table?
explanation: border-spacing sets the distance between borders of adjacent table cells.

question: Which property collapses table borders into a single border?
explanation: border-collapse determines whether table cells have shared or separate borders.

question: Which property controls the visibility of an element without removing its layout space?
explanation: visibility: hidden hides an element without removing it from the document layout.

question: Which property sets the foreground color of text in an element?
explanation: color sets the color of text and text decorations.

question: Which property sets the style of an element's top border?
explanation: border-top-style sets the line style for the top border.

question: Which property sets the width of an element's right border?
explanation: border-right-width sets the thickness of the right border.

question: Which property sets the color of an element's bottom border?
explanation: border-bottom-color sets the color of the bottom border.

question: Which property sets the style of an element's left border?
explanation: border-left-style sets the style of the left border.

question: Which property specifies the alignment of flexible items on the cross-axis?
explanation: align-items aligns items along the cross axis.

question: Which property specifies whether flexible items should wrap or not?
explanation: flex-wrap specifies whether items wrap onto multiple lines.

question: Which property specifies the initial main size of a flex item?
explanation: flex-basis sets the initial main size of a flex item.

question: Which property specifies how much a flex item will grow relative to others?
explanation: flex-grow sets the flex grow factor of a flex item.

question: Which property specifies how much a flex item will shrink relative to others?
explanation: flex-shrink sets the flex shrink factor of a flex item.

question: Which property specifies the order of a flexible item relative to its siblings?
explanation: order specifies the order to lay out an item in a flex or grid container.

question: Which property sets the row gutter in grid or flex layouts?
explanation: row-gap sets the gap between an element's rows.

question: Which property sets the column gutter in grid or flex layouts?
explanation: column-gap sets the gap between an element's columns.

question: Which property sets the grid item's column start and end lines simultaneously?
explanation: grid-column is a shorthand for grid-column-start and grid-column-end.

question: Which property sets the grid item's row start and end lines simultaneously?
explanation: grid-row is a shorthand for grid-row-start and grid-row-end.

question: Which property specifies named grid areas an item spans across?
explanation: grid-area specifies a grid item's size and location within a grid.

question: Which property controls automatic row placement algorithm in CSS Grid?
explanation: grid-auto-flow controls how the auto-placement algorithm places items.

question: Which property sets the vertical alignment of an inline or table-cell element?
explanation: vertical-align sets the vertical alignment of an inline, inline-block or table-cell box.

question: Which property controls whether text should break inside words?
explanation: word-break specifies soft wrap opportunities between characters.

question: Which property controls hyphenation of words when text wraps across lines?
explanation: hyphens specifies how words should be hyphenated when text wraps across multiple lines.

question: Which property controls how font size is adjusted across different typefaces?
explanation: font-size-adjust preserves font readability when fallback fonts are used.

question: Which property controls the rendering of kerning pairs in OpenType fonts?
explanation: font-kerning sets the use of the kerning information stored in a font.

question: Which property controls low-level OpenType font feature tags?
explanation: font-feature-settings allows advanced typographic features of OpenType fonts to be toggled.

question: Which property sets the style of an outline around an element?
explanation: outline-style sets the style of an element's outline.

question: Which property sets the width of an outline around an element?
explanation: outline-width sets the thickness of an element's outline.

question: Which property sets the color of an outline around an element?
explanation: outline-color sets the color of an element's outline.

question: Which property sets the space between an outline and the edge or border of an element?
explanation: outline-offset adds space between an outline and an element's edge.

question: Which property sets whether an element reacts to pointer events?
explanation: pointer-events sets whether an element can become the target of pointer events.

question: Which property controls how touch screen gestures like pinch-to-zoom are handled?
explanation: touch-action sets how an element's region can be manipulated by a touchscreen user.

question: Which property creates a multi-column text layout in CSS?
explanation: column-count breaks an element's content into the specified number of columns.

question: Which property sets the width of columns in a multi-column layout?
explanation: column-width sets the ideal column width in a multi-column layout.

question: Which property sets the vertical rule line drawn between columns in multi-column layout?
explanation: column-rule draws a vertical dividing line between columns.

question: Which property allows an element to span across all columns in a multi-column layout?
explanation: column-span: all makes an element span across all columns.

question: Which property sets the space between columns in multi-column text?
explanation: column-gap sets the horizontal gap between columns.

question: Which property sets the list item marker style for an ordered or unordered list?
explanation: list-style-type sets the marker (such as a disc, character, or counter number) for a list item.

question: Which property specifies an image to use as the list item marker?
explanation: list-style-image specifies an image that will be used as the list item marker.

question: Which property specifies whether list item markers appear inside or outside the content flow?
explanation: list-style-position sets whether the ::marker appears inside or outside the list element box.

question: Which CSS pseudo-element targets the marker box of a list item?
explanation: The ::marker pseudo-element selects the marker box of a list item, which typically contains a bullet or number.

question: Which property defines how an element resizes its content to fit its box (similar to background-size)?
explanation: object-fit sets how the content of a replaced element like or

question: Which property sets the alignment of replaced content within its box when using object-fit?
explanation: object-position determines the alignment of the replaced element inside its box.

question: Which property controls whether an element will be painted when it is not in the viewport?
explanation: content-visibility: auto skips rendering off-screen elements, dramatically improving initial page load performance.

question: Which property sets the estimated size of an element when content-visibility: auto skips its rendering?
explanation: contain-intrinsic-size gives an element a placeholder size to avoid scrollbar jumping when off-screen.

question: Which property specifies that an element and its contents are independent of the rest of the document tree?
explanation: The contain property allows an author to indicate that an element and its contents are, as much as possible, independent of the rest of the tree.

question: Which property sets the style of an element's text underline (e.g. wavy or dotted)?
explanation: text-decoration-style sets the style of the lines specified by text-decoration-line.

question: Which property sets the color of an element's text underline independently of font color?
explanation: text-decoration-color sets the color of decorations added by text-decoration-line.

question: Which property sets the thickness of an element's text underline?
explanation: text-decoration-thickness sets the stroke thickness of the decoration line that is used on text.

question: Which property sets the offset distance of an underline from its text baseline?
explanation: text-underline-offset sets the offset distance of an underline text decoration line from its normal position.

question: Which property controls the position of the underline relative to text descendants?
explanation: text-underline-position specifies the position of the underline line used in text decoration.

question: Which property sets how white space inside an element is handled?
explanation: white-space sets how white space inside an element is handled.

question: Which property sets the tab size (in characters or spaces) in preformatted text?
explanation: tab-size sets the width of a tab character (U+0009).

question: Which property controls whether line breaks are forbidden or allowed within words for Asian text?
explanation: line-break sets how breaking rules are applied to Chinese, Japanese, and Korean (CJK) text.

question: Which property controls the alignment of the last line of a block or a line right before a forced line break?
explanation: text-align-last sets how the last line of a block or a line right before a forced line break is aligned.

question: Which property sets the orientation of the text in a line?
explanation: text-orientation sets the orientation of the text characters in a line.

question: Which property sets the appearance of emphasis marks on text characters?
explanation: text-emphasis applies emphasis marks to text (except spaces and control characters).

question: Which property specifies the indentation of the first line in a block of text?
explanation: text-indent sets the length of empty space that is put before lines of text in a block.

question: Which property controls how an element's text is justified when text-align: justify is set?
explanation: text-justify sets which justification method should be applied when text-align: justify is used.

question: Which property sets how the text rendering engine optimizes speed, legibility, or geometric precision?
explanation: text-rendering provides information to the rendering engine about what to optimize for when rendering text.

question: Which property controls text wrapping across lines in modern CSS (e.g. balance or pretty)?
explanation: text-wrap controls how text inside an element wraps, supporting keywords like balance and pretty.
